findings.reason: the node's brief says to embed a one-line renderer at every call site, which reproduces the fragility the renderer was introduced to remove; a deep helper returning clause-plus-params would change what the node writes and what its test asserts.
findings.text: the render-and-bind block (`prefix_clause = render_path_prefix_clause(alias,"prefixes"); params["prefixes"] = list(path_prefixes)`) is copy-pasted today at claim_paths_for_file_scan (graph_ops.py:141), has_pending_scan_work (graph_ops.py:566), and the plan adds the identical block to claim_files_for_triage (graph_ops.py:279), claim_files_for_enrichment (graph_ops.py:362), claim_files_for_scoring (graph_ops.py:446), the ingest claim (imas_codex/discovery/code/workers.py:526) and has_pending_triage_work/enrich_work/score_work/code_work/link_work (graph_ops.py:593-670) — eleven sites, each separately binding the parameter name the renderer was handed, so a caller that changes the alias or the param string silently detaches the clause from its `$prefixes` binding; one helper owning both the clause and its parameters would hide the mechanism behind a single interface and delete nine hand-written blocks

findings.reason: these take a single caller-computed prefix rather than a user-supplied list, so folding them into the list renderer is a different operation; naming them would let the author state the renderer's scope instead of claiming the tree holds only one, but no code change follows.
findings.text: the plan asserts render_path_prefix_clause is the one renderer for the path-prefix predicate, but other path-prefix predicates remain spelled by hand and are not named anywhere in §14: `n.path STARTS WITH $path_prefix` at domain_queries.py:545 and :591, `n.path STARTS WITH $prefix` at imas_codex/llm/server.py:1034, and, inside the renderer's own module, the graph_search DSL's `__starts_with` operator (query_builder.py:48)

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the path-prefix scope is spread as a repeated render-then-bind block across the existing two sites and the nine functions the code-claims node adds, so the renderer hides the clause but not its parameter and every site can desync them.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan's claim that render_path_prefix_clause is the single renderer for the path-prefix predicate is narrower than the tree: several other path-prefix predicates remain uncited, so the author should state the renderer's scope.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the remaining sections reuse existing CLI options (--root, --reset-to, --path-prefix, --min-score, --focus) and the section names what it retires (seed_missing_roots, create_child_paths), so no unaccounted surface is added.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the code and cites the owners it extends (render_path_prefix_clause, reset_to_status, create_nodes ON CREATE SET, seed_facility_roots) and explicitly names the one caller it declines to convert (the signals scanner filter keeps extra_filter).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no wrapper is proposed over existing machinery; the code-claims node extends the claims and predicates in place and the seed reuses create_nodes' create-only path rather than layering beside it.
